newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mixed, pre-report trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mixed, pre-report trade.

text.p: CBOT soyoil and soymeal futures ended mixed Wednesday on position squaring before the government's acreage and stocks report on Monday, traders said.
"We mostly saw evening up before the report," said a soy trader. "Today (Wednesday) was really quiet."
The U.S. Department of Agriculture is slated to release 1997 plantings data and quarterly grain stocks data on Monday.
The CBOT markets will also be closed Friday in observance of the Good Friday holiday. The upcoming closure also contributed to the slow trading pace, traders said.
Soymeal prices were supported by ongoing talk that U.S. soymeal was being shipped from the U.S. Gulf to western Europe, traders said.

The outbreak of foot and mouth disease in Taiwan hogs was also seen as supportive to soymeal. Many in the U.S. expect hog producers here to increase production in an attempt to capture share in export markets. Consequently, U.S. hog producers likely will need more soymeal for feed rations.
CBOT soymeal ended down $1.90 to up $2.00 per ton, with May down $0.50 at $276.70. Soyoil settled down 0.10 to up 0.10, with May up 0.10 at 24.25 cents per lb.
In soymeal trading, Cargill sold 400 lots March and bought 100 lots May and 100 lots December. Griffin Trading bought 500 lots March, and Refco bought 200 lots December, traders said.
In soyoil trade, Cargill bought 200 lots May and 200 lots July. Tenco bought 300 lots May. Merrill Lynch sold 300 lots May.

Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 15,000 lots, below Tuesday's actual volume of 17,933 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 13,000 lots, against Tuesday's final volume of 16,310, according to CBOT data.
